messages:
alex: noticing a spike of node flaps in us-west-2 -- several serving pods crashed with CUDA illegal memory access. first saw on canary pool ~4387658900.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #4387659 - gfx-node-flap - Sev2 - auto-detected 4387659000

mike: digging logs now. getting repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` from process pid=2248 in runtime-worker. stack shows misaligned addr in pagewalk path. sample:```
E cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7fffd234 - runtime.cc:412 handle_kernel
backtrace:
  serving::kernel::pagewalk()+0x3f
  serving::runtime::dispatch()+0x1a2
```

sarah: are these all same instance type? looks like `g4dn.xlarge` pool and a few `p3` leftovers. also seeing sudden OOMs on some containers before the illegal access log.

devon: OOMs then illegal access suggests a race in buffer management (kvcache / eviction). can we cordon the affected nodes and failover?

julie: started cordon on node usw2-gpu-07 (kubectl cordon usw2-gpu-07) and evicting pods. note: a Dedicated customer had requests routed to that node. putting them on fallback model pool.

alex: routing policy switched to fallback models for affected customers. added temporary route: `route set --pool=fallback-small --match=customer:dedicatedA`

mike: core dumps uploaded to /var/logs/infra/crashdumps/4387659/. attaching kernel oops excerpt:```
[  1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=2248: NVRM has executed an illegal memory access.
[  1234.568000] BUG: misaligned address in pagewalk (addr=0x7fffd234)
```

devon: can we repro on staging with memory pressure? setting up a stress test that allocates large KV caches + concurrent reloads. staging gpu node will be pinned to same driver version.

sarah: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated customers experienced 5-20s tail-latency spikes; 3 requests failed with 500s. most traffic retried successfully after failover. logging a tentative impact window 4387658800-4387659200.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF at 4387660000 - oncall-rotation now primary.

oncall-rotation: taking over. summary pls?

alex: summary: nodes flapped due to CUDA illegal memory access preceded by container OOMs. mitigation: cordoned nodes, evicted pods, routes shifted to fallback pools, crashdumps collected. running repro in staging.

oncall-rotation: ok. escalations? we should involve infra-kernel and hw-vendor if repro.

devon: kernel team @mike please share the nv driver + kernel versions. I see driver 470.141.03 and kernel 5.10.47. also nv-hostpagewalk patches recently rolled to some pools.

mike: confirmed driver/kernel on affected: nvidia-driver=470.141.03, kernel=5.10.47-rt. also note a live paging patch landed yesterday on serving-runtime that touched buffer alignment code (commit: `align-kvcache-handles`). tagging the PR: https://git.internal/r/repro/align-kvcache-handles

julie: rollback option: we can undo the `align-kvcache-handles` rollout (it was a progressive rollout last 12h). if repro points to that change, we should rollback canary immediately.

devon: running a gated rollback on canary now: `kubectl set image deployment/serving-runtime canary=serving-runtime:prev`

alex: telemetry: CPU and GPU mem usage on the node spiked right before crashes; also ephemeral container memory ballooned. logs show repeated `kvcache_evict()` calls concurrently.

oncall-rotation: prepare incident channel note for customers. Sarah pls draft brief impact note and mitigations. include that we rerouted, cordoned nodes, and are investigating root cause.

sarah: draft: "We're investigating brief service disruptions in us-west-2 between ~4387658800 and 4387659200 that caused elevated latencies and a small number of failed requests for some Dedicated customers. We cordoned affected nodes, rerouted traffic to fallbacks, and are collecting crash dumps. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation plan." ack? :thumbsup:

mike: repro in staging: after running concurrent reloads + mem pressure, we hit same `illegal memory access` within ~3 minutes. core shows misaligned pointer from pagewalk path that appears only when eviction and reload interleave. suspect a race where buffer metadata is freed while a kernel pagewalk is in flight.

devon: priority action: block the problematic code path with an extra refcounting guard and re-deploy to canary. i can hotfix and run fast canary.

julie: we also need to increase eviction thresholds as a short-term mitigation to reduce churn: `kvcache.eviction.threshold=0.85` -> 0.92 on affected pools. making change now.

incident-bot: HOTFIX DEPLOY INITIATED 4387661200 - patch id hf-4387

devon: hotfix applied to canary and small fallback pools. monitoring.

mike: after hotfix, stress run in staging for 15m shows no repro. metrics look stable. pushing to broader pool in 10m.

oncall-rotation: keep canary for 30m before full rollout. if no issues, uncordon and gradually reintroduce nodes.

alex: uncordon plan: `kubectl uncordon usw2-gpu-07` then allow node to rejoin for at least 5 minutes before routing dedicated traffic.

sarah: customer note updated with mitigation and ETA for follow-up RCA. will open support tickets for the 3 failed requests.

julie: after 35m canary looks clean. starting gradual rollout to the rest of the pool.

mike: ongoing: capturing more heap snapshots and tracing pagewalk call paths to propose a permanent kernel/runtime fix. will coordinate with kernel team and NV vendor if needed.

devon: next steps: 1) merge stronger refcount guard + tests; 2) add e2e chaos test that simulates concurrent eviction+reload; 3) postmortem doc with timeline and customer impact.

oncall-rotation: thanks all. leaving channel open for RCA updates. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE #4387659 - Mitigated 4387662200 - Next: RCA in 24h

alex: filing postmortem ticket and linking crash dumps and repro logs: https://infra.internal/pm/4387659

sarah: copying customer comms to support tickets. will follow up once RCA is ready.

opsbot: Reminder: please run `kubectl describe node usw2-gpu-* | grep -i docker` and attach any machine-level traces to the ticket.

julie: leaving note: we should also audit driver rollouts across pools; can't rely on single driver/patch combo. assigning infra-kernel to do a sweep.

mike: assigning follow-ups: `@devon` implement guard + tests, `@mike` kernel trace + nv vendor contact, `@sarah` customer comms, `@julie` rollout audit.

devon: acknowledged.

alex: thanks team. closing thread for active mitigation. will reopen if we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
